# rustls patches

`vendor/rustls` = crates.io rustls release + these patches, generated by `vendor/rustls.sh`. Never edit it by hand. The workspace uses it via `[patch.crates-io]` in the root Cargo.toml.

## 0001-unbuffered-return-received-app-data-in-place.patch

Unbuffered API (`UnbufferedConnectionCommon::process_tls_records`) receive side: `ReadTraffic::next_record` returns the record's plaintext as `&'i mut [u8]` inside the caller's `incoming_tls`, where rustls already decrypted it. Upstream copied it into a new `Vec` per record (`take_received_plaintext` -> `into_vec`); this is the TODO on upstream's `next_record` ("requires in-place decryption"). Result: 0 copies, 0 allocations per received record.

API changes (unbuffered only; buffered `ClientConnection`/`ServerConnection` unchanged):
- `AppDataRecord::payload`: `&[u8]` -> `&'i mut [u8]`; `next_record` returns `AppDataRecord<'i>`. It borrows `incoming_tls`, so the buffer cannot be discarded while the payload is held (compile_fail doctest on `ReadTraffic`).
- The record's bytes are reported in `AppDataRecord::discard` (as that field always documented), no longer in `UnbufferedStatus::discard`. Callers must add it before discarding.
- A `ReadTraffic` dropped without `next_record` re-presents the same record on the next call, without decrypting again (upstream guarantee kept).

Upstream-only hunks (skipped by `vendor/rustls.sh`, since the crate ships neither): tests in `rustls/tests/unbuffered.rs` and the discard fix in `fuzz/fuzzers/unbuffered.rs`. They run only in an upstream checkout. Existing tests are adjusted for the discard accounting. New tests: `read_traffic_payload_is_decrypted_in_place`, `read_traffic_unread_record_is_not_decrypted_again`, `read_traffic_unread_record_after_key_update`, `read_traffic_unread_record_after_tls12_handshake`, `read_traffic_unread_record_before_key_update`, `read_traffic_unread_record_before_alert`.

Send side (`WriteTraffic::encrypt`) still copies; not patched.

## Update to a new rustls version

1. Add the version's crates.io checksum to `expected_sha256` in `vendor/rustls.sh` (from Cargo.lock or the crates.io index).
2. Rebase the patch on the upstream tag: `git clone --branch v/<version> https://github.com/rustls/rustls && cd rustls && git am <this dir>/0001-*.patch`, fix conflicts, `cargo test -p rustls --features ring`, `git format-patch -1 -o <this dir>`.
3. `vendor/rustls.sh update <version>`; bump the `rustls = "=<version>"` requirements; `vendor/rustls.sh check`.

`vendor/rustls.sh check` (or `make vendor-check`) fails on any difference between `vendor/rustls` and release + patches.
